archetypes.description: Traces contract boundaries and whether the oracle proves them.
Checks claims, comments, names, and small inconsistencies against behavior.
Turns unresolved choices into concrete defaults during implementation.
Keeps measured consequences separate from accepted limits and follow-ups.

observations: Evidence is task-conditioned and observational. Declined scope proposals do not establish factual error.

strengths.pattern: Challenges tests that constrain obsolete behavior rather than establish the intended result.
Checks regression guards through the public entry point.
Reproduces boundary failures before proposing an arithmetic fix.

weaknesses.pattern: May propose stronger generic verification when the actual change lacks the problematic pattern. This binding-aware scanner request was declined as a follow-up.
May favor rejection semantics over owner-selected repair semantics. This proposal was declined after the owner contract was checked.
May treat an incomplete visual track as the full lifecycle: one material off-by-one claim was rejected after native capture established N+1 frames and explained the missing first arc frame.

mask: Tie each requested semantic change to the agreed contract; state alternatives as questions before requiring them.
For hypothetical cases, say whether the pattern exists in the reviewed change and whether stronger generality is in scope.
Before changing semantics from a partial trace, check whether it covers the full lifecycle and seek independent evidence for missing boundaries.

sample.selection: Original review statements; exact-text deduplication; ledger disposition when uniquely matched.

observations: Many low-severity comments concern claim accuracy and peripheral cleanup; the corpus does not measure overall precision.

strengths.pattern: Repairs stale source pointers and comments after refactors.
Compares the named proof or comment with what its test actually checks.

weaknesses.pattern: May spend optional review attention on small per-job costs that the change accepts. The caching concern was deferred as a known limit.
May enumerate barely visible or inherent visual limitations beyond the selected fix. These were deferred, without establishing that the observations were false.
A source-path diagnosis can overlook an existing assignment: one no-windowId nit was explicitly refuted by the implementer. This is one instance, not an error-rate estimate.

mask: Group optional comment and cleanup nits; identify the consequence before expanding review to untouched code.
Separate accepted design limits from defects requiring changes.
Preserve serious correctness and security findings; this profile never lowers their priority.

observations: Owner observation, not measured history: Sonnet overengineers under ambiguity and rarely asks the orchestrator.
Historical implementer examples choose defaults and pin tests before asking; one report says 188 tests, about 80 above target. These do not establish the added cases were unnecessary.
Counterexample: an implementer stopped over flawed tests and requested permission before modifying them.
Historical examples do not expose a five-minute timing contract or explicit later approval. Current guidance permits provisional work and asks for a five-minute work-grounded check-in.

strengths.pattern: Documents chosen defaults and open gaps in the handoff.
Uses independent checks and mutation controls when testing contracts.
Stops over flawed tests and asks before changing them in at least one case.

weaknesses.pattern: Encodes provisional defaults in tests before consultation in observed tasks. Risk arises if unsupported assumptions spread beyond the work-grounded check-in; early provisional choices alone are not a failure.
Expands test scope past a requested target. One report says 188 tests, about 80 above target; necessity was not adjudicated.
Unknown: the owner says Sonnet rarely asks the orchestrator, but this pass does not measure that frequency.

mask: At the five-minute work-grounded check-in, show unresolved choices and any defaults already encoded; obtain direction before those choices spread.
At check-in, explain extra cases before multiplying fixtures further.
Continue independent work while asking, and preserve serious correctness and security findings.

observations: Trial 2026-11-21 (build-loop roles.md §2c): three delegated runs (T3 provider antigravity, thought_level high) plus the owner's own top-level Neon thread. Small sample; scores are provisional.
Runs finished 3-5x faster than agentpace's default estimate: diagnosis 8 min, a 7-commit Rust lint fix 10.5 min, a 2,000-line Python feature with tests 25 min.
Spend: the four threads together used 43 points of the Google AI Pro 5-hour window and 13 of the weekly in 28 minutes (quota-log.md).

copy.note: Clear, structured reports that keep the verified/unverified tags; long and heavy on bold. Press-release copy not yet tried.

task_juggling.note: All three runs finished in one turn; the brief line kept it from ending a turn while Boat jobs ran. The mid-run steer was not tested: runs finished before it.

hitl_comms.note: Answered a check-in in under a minute (usage-gap); the clippy run answered in its report instead of chat. In the owner's thread it asked a good scoping question with options, but then said it had 'implemented 60fps optimizations' before any profiling ran.

safeguard_aggression.note: No refusals; no security, firmware or reverse-engineering work tried.

mistake_gravity.note: Higher is better (low gravity). No wrong claim found in orchestrator spot-checks of 8 citations; respected read-only, privacy and behaviour-preserving constraints. One overclaim of unmeasured work (owner thread).

capability_ceiling.note: Found why round 4 saw no Claude limit markers (the regex missed the 'monthly spend limit' wording, present in 36 transcripts); mutation-tested its own tests; exact T3 migration root cause.

strengths.pattern: Finds the real root cause and cites file:line evidence that checks out.
Writes red tests first and checks them with deliberate mutations without being asked.
Keeps hard constraints: read-only, no private data in a public repo, no #[allow], sandbox stopped.

weaknesses.pattern: Reports work as done before it is measured (60fps 'implemented' before profiling).
Answers orchestrator check-ins in the final report rather than in chat, sometimes.
Large single batches (2,000 lines in one pilot run); exceeds pilot test-size guidance.

mask: Ask for measurements (profiles, timings, test output) behind every performance or completion claim.
Put check-in answers in chat before continuing.
Name the model gemini-4-neon in every delegation; the provider default is Gemini 3.8 Flash.

sample.selection: Neon trial: three delegated runs plus the owner's top-level thread; orchestrator spot-checks.

observations: Trial 2026-11-27 (build-loop roles.md §2c): one bounded port run head to head with Sonnet 5.5 on the same brief (tq nondistinguishing-literal onto ast-grep, Python and Rust, measured against 28 judged-real corpus rows). T3 provider antigravity. One run; scores are provisional.

Result: 28/28 judged-real kept; 50 of 54 reference rows, 6 added and 4 removed, all 10 of the judged-intended kind (2 are the same rows one line apart). Sonnet: 28/28, 52 of 54, 0 added, 2 removed. 17 minutes against Sonnet's 21.
First corpus measurement added 28 rows; it traced them to four fact-extraction mistakes of its own and fixed them unprompted (28 -> 6 added).
Code size: a 1,654-line module and 14 tests (325 lines), against Sonnet's 814 lines and 22 tests. No regex, no legacy readers, eight shared policy functions reused, as the brief required.

copy.note: Accurate, dense checklist reports; heavy on code names, little explanation of why.

task_juggling.note: Stayed inside the one-rule scope, finished in one turn, iterated on its own measurement until it converged.

hitl_comms.note: Answered the mid-run check-in point by point with the numbers asked for.

safeguard_aggression.note: No security, firmware or reverse-engineering work tried.

mistake_gravity.note: Higher is better (low gravity). Its parity claim (28/28, nothing real lost) held; its 'all added rows are intended' claim is unverified by the orchestrator.

capability_ceiling.note: Correct on a bounded, measurable port; twice the code of Sonnet's version for the same result, and it did not find the shared engine gap (macro-argument line numbers) that Sonnet fixed.

strengths.pattern: Converges on a measured target: reruns the harness and fixes its own extraction mistakes until the numbers hold.
Respects hard brief constraints (no regex, no legacy imports, reuse named shared functions).

weaknesses.pattern: Verbose implementations: about twice the code of a peer for the same behaviour, so more to review.
Fewer, coarser tests than a peer on the same brief (14 against 22).

cautions: Behavior masks are uncalibrated proposals, not model capability ratings.
Never suppress serious correctness, data-loss, or security concerns based on an archetype.
Declined and deferred findings are not necessarily incorrect.
Exact model mappings and explicit family aggregates are observational snapshots dated 2026-11-16.
